items.title: Fire Contained at Garment Factory Along Nairobi-Mombasa Highway
items.description: Property worth millions of shillings was destroyed in a fire at a garment factory in Mavoko, with emergency teams containing the blaze and reporting no injuries.
content: NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 16 – Property worth millions of shillings was destroyed after a fire broke out late Sunday night at a garment factory in Mavoko, along the Nairobi-Mombasa Highway.

The blaze prompted a multi-agency emergency response involving the Kenya Red Cross Society, Mavoko and Machakos County fire teams, Nairobi City County firefighters, the National Youth Service (NYS) and the Kenya Police.
The Kenya Red Cross said its Machakos Action Team joined the other agencies in responding to the incident, which was successfully contained.
“The fire has been contained, and no injuries were reported,” the humanitarian organisation said in an update.
The fire destroyed property valued at millions of shillings, although the exact extent of the losses had yet to be established.

Political commentator Nuru Okanga hospitalised after roadside attack by unknown assailants
items.description: The Mt Kenya Times Okanga shared photographs of his injuries on Sunday, vowing his spirit remained unbroken and that he would not be silenced. By John Kamau Political commentator Nuru Okanga was yesterday attacked by unknown assailants on his way home and hospitalised with visible facial injuries, sharing photographs of his condition on Facebook and vowing that those behind the assault would not succeed in silencing him. Okanga disclosed the attack in a Sunday post accompanied by photographs showing him bleeding, with a large bandage covering one side of his face near the eye and significant swelling across his features. He did not disclose the location of the attack, the number of assailants involved or what may have prompted it, and it was not immediately clear whether he had reported the matter to police. “I have been attacked by unknown people on my way home. I am currently in hospital,” he wrote. He suggested the assault was intended to silence him, but said his resolve remained firm. “They may have wanted to silence me, but God is my protector. I thank Him for the gift of life. My faith remains unshaken, my spirit is strong, and my journey continues,” he added, invoking Isaiah 54:17 — “No weapon formed against me shall prosper.” He closed his post with a declaration that carried clear political undertones. “We shall not be intimidated, we shall not surrender. God is not finished with me yet! ALUTA CONTINUA! WANTAM!” The attack on a prominent political voice, with no suspects identified and no police statement issued, raises urgent questions that cannot go unanswered.

items.title: EU Pays KSh 190k Per Month to Kenyans to Study Master's in Europe: How to Apply
items.description: Kenyan graduates can secure a fully funded Erasmus Mundus scholarship: €1,400 monthly, with tuition, insurance and travel covered. 2027–2029 deadlines vary.
content: PAY ATTENTION: Mark TUKO.co.ke as a preferred source, and our content will appear higher in your Google feed!

The European Union is offering Kenyan graduates a fully funded opportunity to pursue a master's degree at universities across Europe, with a monthly stipend of €1,400 (approximately KSh 196,000) for the duration of their studies.

The Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters (EMJM) scholarship programme, which covers tuition fees, health insurance, and contributions towards travel and relocation costs, is among the most comprehensive study-abroad funding options available to Kenyan students.
Applications for the 2027–2029 intake are currently open.

Rather than a single university or programme, Erasmus Mundus is a collection of over 200 joint master's programmes, each delivered by a consortium of at least three universities across three European countries.

Scholars earn joint or multiple degrees and complete their studies in different countries, gaining international academic exposure.
The monthly €1,400 stipend is paid for every month of study, whether the programme runs for 12, 18, or 24 months.

Over a two-year master's, that amounts to €33,600 in living support. The package also includes a full waiver of tuition and participation fees, health insurance, and a contribution towards travel and installation costs.
Students should, however, budget separately for visa fees and initial accommodation deposits, as the first stipend instalment may not arrive before those early expenses fall due.
There is no single centralised application. Each consortium runs its own process through its own portal, so applicants must apply directly to the programmes they wish to join.
The starting point is the official Erasmus Mundus catalogue , which lists every funded programme alongside its academic focus, participating universities, and application deadline.

Experts advise shortlisting three to five programmes and submitting multiple applications, as competition is intense.
Deadlines for the 2027 intake vary by programme. Neurasmus, which focuses on neuroscience, closes on December 1, 2026.
EMMIR, covering migration and intercultural relations, has a deadline of December 20, 2026.
GLOBE, focused on biodiversity and conservation, closes on January 4, 2027, while InterMaths, spanning mathematics, physics, and engineering, closes on February 17, 2027.
Applicants must hold a bachelor's degree or a recognised equivalent by the time of application.
Those who have previously received an Erasmus Mundus scholarship for a master's or doctoral programme are not eligible to apply again under the same scheme.
Each consortium sets its own academic requirements, including minimum grade thresholds, discipline prerequisites, and English proficiency conditions.
Standard application documents include academic transcripts, degree certificates, a curriculum vitae, a motivation letter, and two or three academic references.
Some programmes additionally request a research proposal, a portfolio, or evidence of relevant work experience.

Kenyan graduates who have previously won the scholarship stress that academic excellence, while helpful, is not the only deciding factor.

One past recipient noted that "you don't have to be a first-class student to secure scholarships like the Erasmus," pointing instead to a well-tailored motivation letter and credible academic references as the most critical elements.
Starting the application process at least three to four months before the relevant deadline is strongly advised.

Kenyans have until Friday, November 20, 2026, at 5:00 pm to submit their views on the government's proposed spending and borrowing plans for the 2027/28 financial year, following a notice issued by the Clerk of the National Assembly on Monday, November 16, 2026.
The notice, issued under Article 118(1)(b) of the Constitution, invites members of the public and stakeholders to submit memoranda on two documents: the 2027 Budget Policy Statement.

According to the National Treasury's October 2026 draft, total proposed spending for the 2027/28 financial year stands at KSh 5.323 trillion.
Of that, KSh 929.1 billion is earmarked for domestic borrowing and KSh 423.8 billion from external lenders, bringing total projected borrowing to KSh 1.321 trillion.
Recurrent expenditure accounts for the largest portion of the budget at KSh 4.02 trillion, while development spending is allocated only KSh 915.8 billion.

The projected fiscal deficit sits at KSh 1.353 trillion. The disparity between recurrent and development spending is expected to draw significant attention from civil society and professional bodies during the submissions period.
Memoranda may be delivered in person to the Office of the Clerk, First Floor, Main Parliament Buildings, Nairobi, or submitted by email to cna@parliament.go.ke.
Submissions must include the name and contact details of the individual or organisation making them.

The four-day window is notably shorter than periods typically allowed for public participation on budget documents, raising concerns about how effectively citizens and organisations can engage before the deadline.
The relevant departmental committees will consider all submissions before presenting their reports to the full House for a vote.

The 2027/28 budget carries particular significance, as it will be the final full budget of President William Ruto's first term, with its borrowing levels, spending balance, and revenue measures likely to shape the economic and political environment heading into the 2027 General Election.

items.title: JIF Circularity Call 2027: Funding and Business Partnership Opportunities for African Circular Economy Enterprises
items.description: African businesses working in plastic waste management, recycling, electronic waste recovery and sustainable manufacturing have an exciting opportunity to
content: African businesses working in plastic waste management, recycling, electronic waste recovery and sustainable manufacturing have an exciting opportunity to develop innovative commercial partnerships with European companies through the Joint Innovation Facility (JIF) Circularity Call 2027 .

The initiative connects African circular economy businesses with European partners to develop commercially viable joint ventures, introduce innovative technologies and scale sustainable business solutions across East and Southern Africa.

Implemented through a collaboration between Project SPARK and SWITCH-2-CE, the initiative aims to improve access to financing, technical expertise, international markets and strategic business partnerships for enterprises operating in the circular economy.
The programme focuses on two priority value chains: plastic packaging and plastic waste, as well as electronics and electronic waste.

Eligible African businesses are encouraged to submit Expressions of Interest before 29 January 2027 . Applicants who successfully pass the initial screening will be invited to submit full grant proposals by 28 February 2027 .
The Joint Innovation Facility Circularity Call is a regional initiative designed to strengthen circular economy businesses through strategic cooperation between African and European companies.

The programme operates under the SWITCH-2-CE in East and Southern Africa Financing Facility, implemented by Expertise France and the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) on behalf of the European Union.
It combines the complementary approaches of Project SPARK and SWITCH-2-CE to address financing and business development challenges affecting circular economy enterprises.
Many African businesses developing sustainable solutions face difficulties accessing appropriate financing, advanced technologies, international markets and experienced business partners.
The JIF Circularity Call seeks to address these barriers by bringing together African entrepreneurs and European companies capable of developing commercially sustainable partnerships.

Through catalytic funding, technical assistance, business connections and market access opportunities, the initiative aims to help promising circular economy solutions move from development and testing towards commercial expansion.
The programme seeks to accelerate the transition towards a more resource-efficient and sustainable economy by supporting commercially viable circular business models.
The initiative places particular emphasis on partnerships that demonstrate clear commercial potential and contribute to measurable environmental and economic benefits.
The JIF Circularity Call concentrates on two priority value chains.
The programme welcomes innovative businesses developing solutions that reduce plastic pollution, improve recycling systems and encourage sustainable packaging.
The second priority value chain focuses on improving the management, recovery and reuse of electronic products and waste.
The call welcomes upstream, midstream and downstream business solutions, with particular interest in upstream and midstream approaches.
This means partnerships addressing sustainable product design, material sourcing, waste prevention, processing and manufacturing are particularly relevant.
The JIF Circularity Call is open to partnerships involving eligible African businesses and European companies.
The lead applicant must be an African for-profit entity legally based in one of the designated priority countries.
Every consortium must include an EU-based for-profit company registered in one of the 27 European Union Member States.
Consequently, eligible African businesses must establish or demonstrate a partnership with a qualifying European company as part of their proposed joint venture.

The initiative combines several forms of support designed to help businesses develop and expand commercially sustainable circular economy solutions.

items.description: Kuwait warns building guards, including Kenyans, they face deportation and a GCC-wide re-entry ban if they fail to report illegal activity on their premises.

Kuwait has warned building guards and caretakers, including Kenyan nationals, that they face administrative deportation and a ban on re-entry if they fail to report illegal or suspicious activity on the properties they oversee.
The warning was issued on November 13, 2026, by a security source and published by the Arab Times.

It fundamentally reframes the guard's role, stating that their responsibility "is not limited to protecting the property but also includes reporting violations and illegal activities occurring within the premises under their supervision."
Israel offers Kenyans, other African nationals KSh 455k, free flights to voluntarily leave country
What raises the stakes considerably is the regional dimension of any deportation.

The security source explained that "GCC security coordination allows information concerning deported individuals to be registered and shared among Gulf Cooperation Council countries," meaning those placed on deportation lists "may consequently face restrictions on entering other GCC countries."

For Kenyan workers, this is not an abstract threat. Kuwait deported 610 expatriates over five days in June 2026 for violating residency and labour laws, with those individuals banned from re-entering Kuwait for life and other GCC states for five years.

A separate incident saw 20 Asian expatriates arrested in a betting den referred for deportation under equivalent conditions. A single infraction in Kuwait can now close doors across Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar, Oman, and Bahrain.

Kenya is among the countries whose nationals work in Kuwait's security sector. By 2025, more than 300,000 Kenyans were employed across Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and the UAE, with additional thousands in Kuwait, Oman, and Bahrain, working in domestic services, hospitality, construction, and security.
US revokes more than 6,000 visas over birth tourism
The building guard role sits at the intersection of property management and law enforcement.
Guards who fail to report a betting den, an unlicensed business, or a residency violation on their premises can now be treated as complicit, regardless of personal involvement.

The November 13 warning coincided with a dawn raid in Jleeb Al-Shuyoukh, where Kuwaiti detectives arrested 14 Asian expatriates at a betting den, all referred to the Administrative Deportation Department.

Kuwait, a country of 4.9 million people, the majority of them foreign nationals, has been intensifying crackdowns on labour and residency violations. The Interior Ministry stated in June 2026 that accountability "targets the worker and the employer alike."

Building guards are advised to familiarise themselves with Kuwaiti reporting channels and escalate any suspected illegal activity promptly. Maintaining records of such reports, including dates, times, and the authorities contacted, adds a layer of protection.
Ensuring that residency and work permits remain valid is equally critical, since the ongoing security campaigns target immigration violations alongside criminal conduct.

For Kenyan households that rely on Gulf remittances, a deportation means an immediate loss of income and the additional costs of repatriation, making compliance not just a legal obligation but a financial necessity.

items.description: Emirates introduces A350 aircraft and Premium Economy on Nairobi–Dubai route Kenya Association of Travel Agents
content: Emirates has introduced its Airbus A350 aircraft on the Nairobi–Dubai route, bringing its Premium Economy cabin to the Kenyan market as the airline expands its premium travel offering on one of its three daily services.

The aircraft entered service on November 12, replacing the Boeing 777 on the morning EK717 flight from Dubai to Nairobi and the return EK718 service. The other two daily rotations between Nairobi and Dubai will continue operating with Boeing 777 aircraft.

The introduction gives passengers travelling from Kenya access to Emirates’ Premium Economy product, which sits between Economy and Business Class and offers an additional cabin choice for travellers seeking greater comfort without paying Business Class fares.
The new offering is particularly relevant to passengers connecting through Dubai to long-haul destinations in Europe and the United States, where Emirates operates an extensive international network.
Speaking about the introduction, Emirates said Kenya had become its second-largest African market by capacity after South Africa, underscoring Nairobi’s importance to its continental operations.
The airline indicated that it would continue assessing opportunities to expand its services in Kenya, with future capacity decisions dependent on passenger demand.

Emirates has positioned Premium Economy as a mid-market product, with fares generally sitting approximately halfway between Economy and Business Class. The airline also indicated that the introduction of the A350 would not, in itself, result in a repricing of fares on the Nairobi route.
The aircraft deployment comes as airlines increasingly differentiate their products across cabin classes to attract passengers with varying travel budgets and preferences.

For travel agents, the introduction creates another option when packaging international travel, particularly for clients travelling to Europe and North America through Dubai. Premium Economy provides an alternative for passengers who want additional comfort on long-haul journeys but may not require the full range of services offered in Business Class.
The introduction further strengthens Emirates’ Nairobi operations and expands the range of international travel products available to passengers departing from Kenya.

items.title: CANEX create-thon, powered by Gebeya, announces nine winners at Afreximbank’s Creative Africa Nexus Weekend (CANEX WKND) 2026
items.description: Sierra Leone Telegraph: 15 November 2026: Nine creators have been named winners across gaming, video and music at CANEX WKND 2026, following the live pitch finale of the CANEX Create-thon, powered …
content: Sierra Leone Telegraph: 15 November 2026:

Nine creators have been named winners across gaming, video and music at CANEX WKND 2026, following the live pitch finale of the CANEX Create-thon, powered by Gebeya. Held on 6 November at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Cultural and Creative Arts in Lagos, the session brought together finalists, industry judges and creative and technology leaders to explore Africa’s opportunities in the artificial intelligence economy.

Organised through the African Export-Import Bank’s (Afreximbank) Creative Africa Nexus (CANEX) programme, in partnership with Gebeya and the Afreximbank Innovation Lab, the competition challenged creators to turn African-inspired ideas into working projects using Gebeya’s Dala Studio.
Participants used AI tools within Dala Studio to produce digital games, videos and music, supported by computing resources and technical guidance.

The session- which also marked the official launch of the Afreximbank Innovation Lab-aimed to demonstrate how access to technology can help African creators turn ideas into AI-powered digital creations, while examining the skills, infrastructure and commercial opportunities needed to build sustainable creative businesses.

Alongside the live pitches, a panel discussion explored the theme, “Claiming Our Stake in the AI Revolution”, bringing forth a much-needed conversation on the opportunities as well challenges of this fast-evolving area, as well as what it means for African creators.

According to Gebeya, around 6,000 creators from 43 countries participated in the competition, submitting 792 games, music tracks and videos built on Dala Studio. The top three creators in each category advanced to the live pitch finale.

Speaking at the opening of the session, Temwa Gondwe, Director, Creatives and Diaspora at Afreximbank, emphasised that Africa’s creative influence must translate into greater ownership and economic returns. He called for affordable computing power, accessible creative tools, effective distribution channels and stronger protection of creators’ intellectual property.
“The question is not whether Africa will participate. The question is how much value Africa will create and own and retain,” Gondwe said.
He highlighted the importance of connecting creators with investors, buyers and audiences, arguing that access to technology must be accompanied by opportunities to build sustainable businesses.

The competition offered a total prize pool of US$50,000. Under its published award structure, first-, second- and third-place prizes in each category are US$7,000, US$3,500 and US$1,500 respectively, with additional awards for qualifying creators from the top 20 African countries.

The live pitch judging panel comprised Oluwasemilore Oludipe, Programmes Manager at Co-creation HUB (CcHUB); Mayenzeke Baza, Chief Investment and Development Officer at CEEIT; and Miebaka Anga, Strategic Partner Manager at YouTube.
Amadou Daffe, Chief Executive Officer and Co-Founder of Gebeya, urged young Africans to move beyond experimenting with AI and use it to create products and services that generate income.
“Knowledge is in the pocket. The question is, what do you do with it?” Daffe said.

He argued that the practical challenge is helping creators recognise and pursue the commercial possibilities of the technology. Drawing on Gebeya’s experience, he highlighted the importance of local-language capabilities and local-currency payment options in making digital tools more accessible to African users.

The panel was moderated by Omolabake Olagunju, Programme Manager at CcHUB Creative Economy. Joining Daffe were Malik Afegbua, Founder of Slick City Media; Uchechi Arinze, Creative Director and Founder of CHéCHI; Ibrahim Tsado Yisa, Africa Director at Udu Technologies; and Oo Nwoye, Founder of TechCircle.

The discussion examined how AI is changing the creation and consumption of creative work, including questions of ownership and originality. Contributions also explored intentional storytelling, cultural representation, algorithmic bias and the cost of accessing digital tools, highlighting the need to consider whose stories are being told and how African cultures are represented.

Emeka Onyia, Afreximbank’s Director, Digital Business and Innovation, described the session as an inaugural activity for the Afreximbank Innovation Lab. He said AI was lowering some of the equipment and production barriers facing creators, while stressing that skills and the effective use of tools remained essential. He also outlined the Lab’s ambition to bring people together to develop ideas and technologies that support African trade.

With a format centred on working projects rather than proposals alone, the Create-Thon combined practical technology access, mentorship and industry exposure. Gebeya also acknowledged IREX’s support for the initiative.

For Afreximbank, the competition forms part of its broader work through CANEX to develop and commercialise Africa’s creative and cultural industries, helping creators reach markets, attract partners and retain more value from their work.

African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank) is a Pan-African multilateral financial institution mandated to finance and promote intra- and extra-African trade. For over 30 years, the Bank has been deploying innovative structures to deliver financing solutions that support the transformation of the structure of Africa’s trade, accelerating industrialisation and intra-regional trade, thereby boosting economic expansion in Africa.

A strong supporter of the African Continental Free Trade Agreement (AfCFTA), Afreximbank has launched a Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS) that was adopted by the African Union (AU) as the payment and settlement platform to underpin the implementation of the AfCFTA.

Working with the AfCFTA Secretariat and the AU, the Bank has set up a US$10 billion Adjustment Fund to support countries effectively participating in the AfCFTA. At the end of December 2025, Afreximbank’s total assets and contingencies stood at over US$48.5 billion, and its shareholder funds amounted to US$8.4 billion.

Afreximbank has investment grade ratings assigned by China Chengxin International Credit Rating Co., Ltd (CCXI) (AAA), GCR (A), Japan Credit Rating Agency (JCR) (A-), Moody’s (Baa2) and S&P Global Ratings (BBB+). The Bank is headquartered in Cairo, Egypt.

items.description: A fire that broke out at a garments factory in Mavoko, Machakos County, along the Nairobi-Mombasa Highway, has been contained, with no injuries reported. In an…
content: A fire that broke out at a garments factory in Mavoko, Machakos County, along the Nairobi-Mombasa Highway, has been contained, with no injuries reported.

In an update on Monday, November 16, the Kenya Red Cross Society said its Machakos Action Team joined several emergency response agencies in containing the fire following a coordinated response involving county and national government teams.
The response brought together fire teams from Mavoko and Machakos County, Nairobi City County, the National Youth Service (NYS), the Kenya Police and the Kenya Red Cross Society.

The humanitarian organisation confirmed that the fire had been contained and no casualties had been reported. It added that an assessment would be conducted later in the day to establish the extent of the damage.
“The fire has been contained and no injuries were reported. An assessment will follow later today,” the organisation stated.
The incident comes days after three people were rescued and taken to hospital following the collapse of a building under construction in Syokimau, Machakos County, on Friday, November 13.
The Kenya Red Cross said search and rescue operations were ongoing for another person who had been reported missing.

“Three people have been rescued and taken to hospital after a building under construction collapsed in Syokimau. Search and rescue operations are ongoing for one person reported missing,” the organisation said.
Its response team worked alongside other emergency agencies to coordinate rescue efforts at the site.
In a separate incident, at least 11 people were rescued after a wall under construction collapsed in Riverside, Nairobi County.
In an update issued on Saturday, November 14, the Kenya Red Cross said it had deployed response teams and two E-Plus ambulances to the scene. Those rescued were taken to hospital for treatment.
Meanwhile, more than 300 households in Tana River County have been affected by flooding after heavy rainfall caused a seasonal river in Wardesa to burst its banks.
The flooding affected residents in Eldera, Kono Ramadha and Mata Wardesa, while the Kono Ramadha-Mlanjo road was cut off, disrupting transport in the area.
The Kenya Red Cross said its teams were on the ground assessing the situation and working with local administrators to alert communities downstream and guide families to safer locations.
The organisation urged residents in affected areas to heed safety advisories as emergency teams continued monitoring the situation.

Data Shows 78% of Kenya’s Building Collapse Deaths Happen on Sites
items.description: Building collapses in Nairobi killed ten in 24 hours. See Stats Kenya data, IEK demands and what Nairobi County says on approvals, audits and enforcement.
content: Nine to ten workers died on Nairobi construction sites between Friday and Saturday, and the data shows the deaths follow a pattern.

Stats Kenya, a data research company, has logged at least 84 building collapses in Kenya since January 2020 , which killed at least 102 people. Nairobi accounts for 31 of those collapses and 39 of the deaths.

The Institution of Engineers of Kenya (IEK) wants investigations and nationwide audits. Nairobi City County says its Development Control Policy 2026 and Integrated Development Plan already target the gaps. For developers, lenders and buyers off plan, the question is whether enforcement now matches the paperwork.

The Eastleigh collapse on 23 October 2026 killed eight, the highest toll in the Stats Kenya dataset. The Syokimau slab failure followed on 13 November, and the Riverside wall failed on 14 November. All three buildings were under construction.

IEK separates the last two: it points to temporary works and concrete placement at Syokimau, and to the excavation support system and retaining walls at Riverside. It says these are “not conclusions on cause or responsibility.”

At Syokimau, police said 405 workers were on site and all were accounted for. Duncan Ochieng, the assistant inspector general of police in charge of disaster management, said: “So far we have confirmed six bodies, but also five people have been rushed to Imara Daima Hospital.”
At Riverside, Nairobi County said 39 workers were on site when the wall gave way, and the Kenya Red Cross sent action teams and ambulances.
Stats Kenya’s figures show where the risk sits. Of 102 deaths, 80 occurred at buildings under construction or demolition. Occupied buildings account for far fewer.

Most victims are workers. Neighbours, passers by and traders also die when a structure falls onto homes, shops and roads. That puts the cost on payrolls, site contractors and insurers before it reaches tenants.
Murang’a recorded the most deaths per collapse. At least four Nairobi collapses fell in Kamukunji Sub County, which includes Eastleigh, Gikomba and Shauri Moyo.

Kenya recorded 5 to 14 collapses a year from 2020 to 2025, with 14 the peak in 2022. By mid November 2026 the count stood at 25 collapses and 38 deaths. Stats Kenya cautions that older reports are harder to find online, so earlier years likely read low. It also notes that 37 of the 84 collapses fell in March to May, the long rains, though most reports give no cause.

The National Construction Authority (NCA) registers contractors and projects. In a 2018 assessment of 14,895 buildings, it found 10,791 needed demolition or strengthening before safe use, and only 2,194 qualified as safe. Its 2020 report counted 87 collapses in the previous five years, with about 200 deaths. In 2022 it inspected 26,060 projects and suspended 18,192, or 69.8%, for failing building regulations.
The 2018 and 2020 figures are reported by The Star .

The county names collapse as a problem in its own policy. The Executive Summary of the Nairobi City County Development Control Policy (final version dated 14 July 2026) lists buildings built without approval, buildings that depart from approval conditions, and the “collapse of buildings due to weak and unstable structures.”
It says the county has deployed technical staff to sub counties, run periodic audits of the built environment and stepped up enforcement.
The plan sets numerical targets for statutory inspections. It budgets KSh 85 million across five years for surveillance and statutory inspections to monitor developments.

Governor Johnson Sakaja addressed Eastleigh directly on 24 October. He said county records show an application for a 15 storey building with a basement was submitted and never granted. In his words: “The application was never granted, meaning there is no approval for this construction.”

He said a change of user application for the plot was approved in 2024, the Urban Planning Committee raised concerns in November 2024, and an enforcement order followed earlier this year. The county sent its documents to the police and the Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) and called for investigation of the architect, physical planner and engineering firm named in its records.

More than 200 files sit at the Director of Public Prosecutions’ office and asked for prosecution powers to return to the county, as KBC reported . Capital FM reported a counter claim: the DPP’s office said City Hall never submitted an inquiry file on the Eastleigh collapse.

IEK addressed national and county governments, the NCA, the Engineers Board of Kenya (EBK), the Directorate of Occupational Safety and Health Services and the National Building Inspectorate. It asked for independent technical investigations, preservation of evidence and a halt to work in affected areas until safety clearance. I

t also asked for registered engineers on design and supervision until the Occupation Certificate issues, risk based audits of high risk projects, and a national review of safety regulations “with clear timelines and public reporting.”

The county’s tools and IEK’s demands overlap on three points: engineer supervision, inspection and enforcement. They differ on who investigates. IEK wants independence and EBK discipline for engineers found culpable. The county has referred matters to police and the DCI.
A project with an approval gap faces stop orders and demolition risk under the county’s planned enforcement rules. Lenders carry that risk on construction loans.

Off plan buyers carry it through delays. Sites that pass inspection keep the permit and Occupation Certificate path open, and the county has tied that certificate to full payment of the Development Impact Fee.

items.title: Somalia vs Ghana AFCON Qualifier prediction: Match preview, team news, current form & h2h
items.description: Ghana and Somalia meet for the second time in four days in the ongoing 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers on Monday evening.
content: Ghana and Somalia meet for the second time in four days in the ongoing 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers on Monday evening.
The Black Stars were 2-0 winners when the two sides met last Thursday, courtesy of goals from Felix Afena-Gyan and Jonas Adjetey.

Following the victory, a first in their quest to qualify for the 2027 AFCON, Ghana are in third place in Group C with three points. Ivory Coast lead the standings with nine points, three more than Gambia in second.
Although Somalia are officially the home team, the match will once again be played at the Essipong Sports Stadium in Ghana, with Somalia unable to host the fixture at a CAF-approved home venue.
Another three points would take the Black Stars to six points and put them firmly back into the qualification battle.
However, they cannot afford to drop many more points because they still have difficult fixtures against the group leaders later in the campaign.
Somalia come into the game rooted to the bottom of the group without a point after losing all three of their fixtures so far.
The first leg win ended Ghana’s 37-month wait for an AFCON qualifying win and gave the new interim technical team a winning start in competitive football.
The Black Stars will now be looking to build momentum by winning the second game of the double-header.
The match kicks off at 6PM E.A.T at the Essipong Sports Stadium
There are no changes expected from the Somalia side that lost last Thursday, with Faisal Othman and Mubashir Nour providing the attacking options up front.
Musa Bile had a couple of chances after coming on as a substitute in the first leg but he may have to settle for a place on the bench.
Ghana have received several major boosts during this international window as Mohammed Kudus returned after a lengthy absence and immediately produced an assist.
Jordan Ayew returned after recovering from a groin injury and is expected to feature in the starting XI.
Mohammed Salisu and Alidu Seidu have also returned to strengthen the defence.
These sides have played against each other three times in their history – with Ghana winning all of the matches.
They have scored nine goals against Somalia and have not conceded any, making them favorites heading into this game.
Ghana have superior squad quality, greater international experience and have already beaten Somalia 2-0 only four days ago. They also desperately need another three points.
An away win is therefore the most straightforward selection for this particular game. Winning to nil also provides and attractive market.

items.title: AFC Leopards target victory against Mombasa United in Kenya Premier league
items.description: AFC Leopards will today, Sunday, November 15, 2026, take on Mombasa United in a Kenyan Premier League encounter as Ingwe seeks to maintain its unbeaten
content: AFC Leopards will today, Sunday, November 15, 2026, take on Mombasa United in a Kenyan Premier League encounter as Ingwe seeks to maintain its unbeaten run and strengthen its position in the 2026/27 season.
The match is scheduled to kick off at 3:30 PM EAT at Wang’uru Stadium, with both sides targeting crucial points for different reasons.

AFC Leopards head into the encounter unbeaten in their opening six league matches, having recorded two victories and four draws. Their 2-0 victory over Kakamega Homeboyz on November 1 was an important result before they settled for a goalless draw against 3K FC on November 7. Ingwe currently has 10 points and occupies third position in the league standings.

Head coach Fred Ambani has emphasised the need for his players to improve their finishing, pointing out that missed scoring opportunities have cost the team valuable points in previous matches. Ambani wants his attacking players to remain composed in front of goal and make better use of the chances created.

On the other hand, Mombasa United head into the fixture under pressure after collecting just one point from their opening six matches. The newly promoted side sits bottom of the 18-team standings, having suffered five defeats and recorded one draw.

In their most recent league outing on November 7, Mombasa United suffered a 3-2 defeat against Shabana at Mbaraki Sports Club. This followed earlier losses against Migori Youth, who beat them 2-0, and KCB, who secured a 3-1 victory.

Assistant coach Mohamed Ahmed Mchulla has revealed that the team has been working on its defensive weaknesses, particularly dealing with set-pieces and maintaining defensive organisation after losing possession. He has also stressed the importance of improving their finishing if they are to start collecting positive results.
Captain Hakimu Msami has also expressed confidence that the players have learned from their previous mistakes and are ready to fight for their first league victory of the campaign.

Meanwhile, AFC Leopards have some injury concerns, with Eric Balecho and Samwel Semo reportedly sidelined, while the fitness of Kayci Odhiambo and Vincent Mahiga remains under assessment. Goalkeeper Tom Ikara will be one of the key players for Ingwe, having kept five clean sheets in the club’s opening six league matches.

The encounter presents an important opportunity for both sides. AFC Leopards will be looking to extend their unbeaten run and remain in contention for the league title, while Mombasa United will be desperate to secure their first victory of the season and move away from the bottom of the table.
All eyes will therefore be on Wang’uru Stadium as the two sides battle for three valuable points.

items.title: San Antonio Spurs streak to 12th win, Lakers roll on
items.description: The San Antonio Spurs were forced to dig deep before defeating the Utah Jazz 110-102 to clinch their 12th straight victory on Monday as the Los Angeles Lakers
content: The San Antonio Spurs were forced to dig deep before defeating the Utah Jazz 110-102 to clinch their 12th straight victory on Monday as the Los Angeles Lakers extended their winning streak to eight games.
Utah, languishing at the bottom of the Western Conference with only one win, had threatened to pull off a huge upset after leading by five points midway through the fourth quarter.
But San Antonio closed with a 16-4 run in the final three minutes to improve to 12-2 at the top of the Western Conference standings, neck-and-neck with the Lakers.
Dylan Harper led San Antonio’s scorers with 31 points, while French star Victor Wembanyama had another big game at both ends with 26 points, 10 rebounds, six assists and five blocks.

Los Angeles kept pace with their rivals from Texas on Sunday after Luka Doncic delivered his seventh 40-point performance of the season in a 131-123 road win over the Phoenix Suns.
Doncic, who is averaging 39 points per game, drained five three-pointers en route to 43 points with nine assists in a wire-to-wire victory.
The Lakers had appeared to be strolling towards a rout after surging into a 31-point lead late in the third quarter.
But they were given a huge scare in the fourth quarter as Phoenix threatened a sensational comeback after closing the gap to just five points.
Despite being outscored 43-27 in the final frame, the Lakers held off the rally to move to 12-2 in the Western Conference.
“We got a little bit sloppy in that fourth quarter so we’ve really got to work on that,” Doncic said.
“I know we’ve got eight in a row, but we’ve got to do better at that.”

With the Lakers still missing the injured Austin Reaves, Doncic was given scoring support from Quentin Grimes, who rattled in five three-pointers in a 22-point haul.
Collin Sexton added 16 from the bench, and Walker Kessler finished with a double-double of 14 points and 12 rebounds.
The Oklahoma City Thunder snapped their three-game losing streak. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored 37 in a 125-103 win at Sacramento.
In the Eastern Conference, LeBron James moved into third place on the NBA’s all-time assists list as the Philadelphia 76ers overpowered the Indiana Pacers 131-124.
James finished with 15 points and 11 assists as the Sixers improved to 11-3.
James is now one ahead of Jason Kidd’s 12,091 career assists. Chris Paul is second on the list with 12,552, while John Stockton leads with 15,806.
“It’s super humbling,” James said.
“It’s something that I didn’t obviously foresee in my career, but assists mean a lot to me — moving the ball, being able to find my team-mates.
THE KING. the greatness continues. 👑 pic.twitter.com/d4uxCkyONE
“And just being linked to some of the greatest to ever play this game, and also a dear friend of mine in JK (Kidd). It’s very special,” James added.

The Sixers remain half a game behind the Boston Celtics at the top of the Eastern Conference. The Celtics cruised to a sixth straight win on Sunday with a 131-94 rout of the Dallas Mavericks at the TD Garden.
Jayson Tatum led the way with 32 points, six rebounds and six assists as the Celtics improved to 11-2.
The reigning NBA champion New York Knicks improved to 7-6 after a 112-108 overtime win against the Toronto Raptors.
Karl-Anthony Towns and Jalen Brunson each scored 28 points for New York.

items.title: England beat Spain in Nations League to end record unbeaten run
items.description: England snapped world champions Spain's record unbeaten run with a 3-2 victory in Madrid on Sunday to clinch the top spot in Nations League group A3.
content: England snapped world champions Spain’s record unbeaten run with a 3-2 victory in Madrid on Sunday to clinch the top spot in Nations League group A3.
Goals from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White inflicted La Roja’s first loss in a competitive game since March 2023, after 44 without defeat.

England’s Elliot Anderson was sent off in the second half as Spain fought back from three goals down with strikes from Mikel Oyarzabal and Nico Williams, but Luis de la Fuente’s World Cup winners could not find the equaliser.
Both sides were already sure to progress, but as group winners England will be seeded for the quarter-finals in March.
Spain had beaten England in the Euro 2024 final before adding a second world crown this summer, while the Three Lions finished third.

Tuchel selected James Trafford in goal over Jordan Pickford and also brought White and Konsa into the side.
Teenage star Lamine Yamal was fit to start for Spain at Atletico Madrid’s Metropolitano stadium after missing their midweek win over the Czech Republic.
However the youngster did not see much of the ball in the first half as England came out strongly.
Spain goalkeeper Unai Simon produced a strong reaction save to deny Jude Bellingham, while Anthony Gordon had a dangerous shot blocked.
Ballon d’Or winner Kane, who beat Yamal to the award, sent an effort narrowly wide.
Barcelona defender Pau Cubarsi handed England the advantage when he clumsily felled Kane in the area on the stroke of half time.
The Bayern Munich hitman powered a perfect penalty past Simon, who dived the right way but to no avail.
De la Fuente tried to react at half-time with a triple change, including throwing on Barcelona duo Fermin Lopez and Pedri, but England quickly found more joy.
Konsa headed home the second from Declan Rice’s corner in the 53rd minute after the Arsenal defender was left unmarked by Spain’s defence.
Four minutes later England sliced open Spain’s defence with Kane and Bellingham combining to set up White for the third.

La Roja clawed their way back into the game when Anderson fouled Yamal in the area as the Spain striker ran in on goal.
The Manchester City midfielder was dismissed and Oyarzabal slotted home the penalty.
Spain found a second when Gordon gave the ball away and Yamal fed Williams, whose shot hit the post and bounced in.
Williams curled over and Trafford superbly denied Yamal and Marc Cucurella as Spain looked fruitlessly for the goal they needed to preserve their unbeaten record.
Including friendlies, Spain had gone 43 straight matches without defeat.

items.description: Sports Mole previews Monday's Nations League clash between Germany and Netherlands, including predictions, team news and possible lineups.
content: By Anthony Nolan | 14 Nov 2026 23:59 , Last updated: 15 Nov 2026 04:46
Fighting for a place in the UEFA Nations League quarter-finals, Germany are set to host League A's Group A2 leaders, the Netherlands , at Olympiastadion Berlin on Monday.
Die Mannschaft know that they likely need to win to progress, while Oranje are through barring an unprecedented swing in goal-difference.
Jurgen Klopp 's Germany are pushing to qualify for the Nations League quarter-finals for just the second time, but they face a tough test to reach the last eight.

Die Mannschaft are currently third in Group A2, level on eight points with Greece and three behind the Netherlands, and their chance to go through leans on the fact UEFA prioritises head-to-head points between tied teams.
Klopp's side were beaten 1-0 by the Azure and White on September 27 before drawing 0-0 with them on matchday four.

However, Ivan Jovanovic's men were hammered 7-0 by the Dutch on Friday, meaning that a German victory over the Netherlands on Monday would see them progress ahead of Greece regardless of their result against Serbia .
Die Mannschaft were held to a 1-1 stalemate by Oranje on matchday one, with Cody Gakpo equalising in second-half stoppage time to deny his former Liverpool manager maximum points.

Klopp's team have remained undefeated in the group since their loss to Greece, most recently beating Serbia 3-1 on Friday, when they raced into a 2-0 lead within the first 14 minutes thanks to an own-goal from Srdjan Babic and a follow-up by Florian Wirtz.
Meanwhile, Xavi 's Netherlands have yet to taste defeat in the Nations League this term, and are in a commanding position at the top of their group going into the final matchday.

Leading with 11 points, Oranje's 7-0 demolition of Greece last time out - following a 2-2 draw on October 1 - means the only possibility of them finishing below the top two is if there is a dramatic 14-goal swing in the Azure and White's favour.

Xavi is without talismanic centre-back Virgil van Dijk this month, but his team were still able to keep their first clean sheet in the competition on Friday, while Tijani Reijnders's first-half hat-trick set the tone at the opposite end of the pitch.
However, it remains to be seen whether the Netherlands can repeat that attacking showcase in Germany, considering that they have won just one of their last six away clashes against Die Mannschaft.

On the other hand, Oranje are unbeaten in their past seven matches on the road, and last suffered a travelling defeat in a penalty shootout against Spain during the Nations League quarter-finals in March 2025, following a 5-5 aggregate draw .
Germany have no new injury issues to contend with, though they are missing Bayern Munich stars Jamal Musiala and Serge Gnabry due to respective muscle problems.
In their absence, Klopp could continue with Brajan Gruda, Florian Wirtz and Derry Scherhant behind Arsenal man Kai Havertz up top.
As for the Netherlands, they were forced to take off Frenkie De Jong at half time against Greece after he suffered back pain, and he has now left the national squad to return to Barcelona.
Teun Koopmeiners looks set to step in and fill the gap alongside Joey Veerman at the base of Xavi's midfield, while Tijani Reijnders operates in the number 10 role.

Further forward, Donyell Malen has been a standout for Roma this season with 12 goals across all competitions, and he will be keen to add to his goal against Greece while Cody Gakpo and Crysencio Summerville provide width.
Captain Virgil van Dijk has sat out this international break with complaints of physical discomfort, so expect to see Tottenham Hotspur's Micky van de Ven and Jan Paul van Hecke start at centre-back.

items.title: EIGHT BARRAMUNDIS TO PLAY IN AUSTRALIA FOLLOWING CAMPAIGN IN KENYA
items.description: Eight Papua New Guinea Barramundis players have secured club cricket opportunities in Melbourne, Australia.
content: Eight Papua New Guinea Barramundis players have secured club cricket opportunities in Melbourne, Australia.
The opportunities will provide them with the chance to gain regular playing experience across three formats of the game.
The announcement was made following the team’s arrival from Kenya, where they competed in the ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup Challenge League A.

PNG captain Assadollah Vala, Aue Oru and Doko Rupa will join Endeavour Hills Cricket Club. John Kariko and Patrick Nou will represent Craigieburn Cricket Club, while Greenvale Kangaroos Cricket Club has secured the services of Lega Siaka and Igo Morea. Boio Ray will represent Narre North Cricket Club.
PNG Barramundis Head Coach Tim McCaskill said the opportunities would be valuable for the players, particularly through exposure to regular competitive cricket.

“We are excited for the player placement opportunities in Melbourne, and the players will benefit from regular play across three formats, which will be a new experience for the majority of them,” he said.
This follows the Barramundis’ unsuccessful campaign in Kenya, where they recorded only one win from five matches.
McCaskill said the outcome was unfortunate, adding that the current 50-over cycle had come to an end.

“Unfortunately, that is the end of the current 50-over cycle. The next focus for players will be playing in the Port Moresby Cricket Association (POMCA). A group of players will have the opportunity to play the summer in Melbourne,” McCaskill said.

Reflecting on the campaign, McCaskill said the results in Kenya had highlighted the increasing standard of cricket among Associate Member countries and the need for PNG to improve its competitiveness.
“The results in Kenya have highlighted to all players that the game across Associate countries has gone up a level,” he added.
“If we are to remain competitive, then we need to make sure that our ability to handle match demands improves.”
He identified playing spin bowling and improving the team’s scoring capacity as key areas requiring attention.

“We are going to be targeted with spin by all teams, so all players have to improve their understanding of playing spin. When to use their feet, using the depth of the crease to score on each side of the wicket, and improving our hitting power to push scoring rates,” McCaskill stated.
The team’s campaign concluded on Saturday, October 31, with an 88-run loss to hosts Kenya. PNG recorded their only victory against Denmark, winning by four wickets on October 25.
PNG opened their campaign against Jersey on Thursday, October 22, suffering a 172-run defeat before bouncing back three days later with a four-wicket victory over Denmark.
However, the Barramundis were unable to maintain their winning momentum, losing their remaining three matches against Qatar, Kuwait and Kenya.
On Tuesday, October 27, PNG suffered a nine-wicket defeat against Qatar before going down by 10 wickets to Kuwait on Friday, October 30.
Their final match against Kenya on Saturday, October 31, ended in an 88-run defeat, concluding their five-match campaign with one victory and four losses.
The results meant PNG did not qualify for the next stage of the ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup qualification pathway, bringing an end to the current 50-over World Cup cycle.

items.title: Kenyan Adtech firm Suss Ads brings ChatGPT advertising to seven African markets
items.description: Suss Ads, the Kenyan advertising technology firm, has launched its ChatGPT advertising solutions in seven African markets. This is a new conversational AI
content: A key element of the Kenyan launch is the integration of M-PESA for campaign funding.

Suss Ads, the Kenyan advertising technology firm, has launched its ChatGPT advertising solutions in seven African markets. This is a new conversational AI channel for brands and agencies who want to be able to reach consumers as they’re actively researching a product. The markets are Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa, Egypt, Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia. There’s also a localised M-PESA payment integration in Kenya to remove the foreign currency hurdle for local advertisers.

Suss Ads was founded in Nairobi in 2021 with the intention of the rollout being a bridge between the global AI platforms and the local commercial infrastructure. As consumers increasingly turn to conversational interfaces to compare services, look at universities, check out financial products and plan their travels, the limitations of interruptive advertising are becoming more and more apparent. Rather than being seen by users as they’re passively scrolling through social media or display ads, Suss Ads will appear in the conversation as the user is actively in the consideration phase of the purchase journey.

As per the rollout plan these ads will be clearly labelled and appear separately from the organic Chatgpt responses so that there is no possibility of advertising paying to influence or alter the platform’s answers and recommendations in any way. They are currently available to eligible adult users on the ChatGPT Free and Go plans and are being offered as an additional layer to the existing digital media mix rather than as a direct replacement.

A key element of the Kenyan launch is the integration of M-PESA for campaign funding. Getting access to international ad networks often involves the use of US dollars and international credit cards which creates a whole host of admin and cash flow issues for the local businesses. Suss Ads removes that barrier by allowing businesses to plan their budgets and pay for their ad spend via mobile money. It’s a massive enabler for SMES who are looking to trial AI driven customer acquisition in conjunction with a well established local partner.
Why you should be polite to ChatGPT, Gemini and other AIs

Beyond payment processing the company offers end to end campaign management covering creative, media and performance. For the multi-national brands operating across North, West, East and Southern Africa the expansion also enables the delivery of coordinated cross border campaigns through the regional partner.

The conversational AI advertising is an extension of Suss Ads’ wider technology stack which over the past 5 years has evolved from traditional digital media buying through to programmatic, rich media, video, connected TV and digital out of home. The stack is built around a number of specialist units which take the consumer from the first point of discovery to the point of conversion. Suss Media is responsible for multi-channel distribution, Suss Studio for the development of interactive creative, Suss Intelligence for the data driven reporting and Suss CX for the automated customer conversations across WhatsApp, Telegram and social.

Suss Ads operates across Kenya, Tanzania and the UAE and works with clients in telecoms, financial services, consumer goods, education, entertainment and technology. The model is to combine global AI advertising inventory with local mobile money infrastructure and local campaign support to help African businesses adapt to the changing way consumers are discovering products and to reach high-intent audiences at the point of decision.

items.title: Kenyans Have 4 Days to Submit Views on Ruto's 2027/28 Budget Plan
items.description: Kenyans can submit views on the 2027 Budget Policy Statement and debt strategy by 20 November, as Parliament reviews proposed KSh 5.323 trillion spending.
content: Search option is now available at TUKO! Feel free to search the content on topics/people you enjoy reading about in the top right corner ;)

Elijah Ntongai is an experienced editor at TUKO.co.ke, with more than four years in financial, business, labour and technology research and reporting. His work provides valuable insights into Kenyan, African, and global trends.

Kenyans have until Friday, November 20, 2026, at 5:00 pm to submit their views on the government's proposed spending and borrowing plans for the 2027/28 financial year, following a notice issued by the Clerk of the National Assembly on Monday, November 16, 2026.
The notice, issued under Article 118(1)(b) of the Constitution, invites members of the public and stakeholders to submit memoranda on two documents: the 2027 Budget Policy Statement.
ODM, UDA and Jubilee Share 79% of KSh 2.26 Billion Political Party Funds for 2025/2026

The statement outlines the government's proposed expenditure priorities for the coming financial year and the Medium-Term Debt Management Strategy, which covers the 2027/28 to 2029/30 period and details how the government plans to finance its budgetary needs while managing the costs and risks of public debt.

According to the National Treasury's October 2026 draft, total proposed spending for the 2027/28 financial year stands at KSh 5.323 trillion.
Of that, KSh 929.1 billion is earmarked for domestic borrowing and KSh 423.8 billion from external lenders, bringing total projected borrowing to KSh 1.321 trillion.
Recurrent expenditure accounts for the largest portion of the budget at KSh 4.02 trillion, while development spending is allocated only KSh 915.8 billion.

The projected fiscal deficit sits at KSh 1.353 trillion. The disparity between recurrent and development spending is expected to draw significant attention from civil society and professional bodies during the submissions period.
Memoranda may be delivered in person to the Office of the Clerk, First Floor, Main Parliament Buildings, Nairobi, or submitted by email to cna@parliament.go.ke.
Submissions must include the name and contact details of the individual or organisation making them.
Kenyans escape KSh 10 fuel price increase in November-December cost

The four-day window is notably shorter than periods typically allowed for public participation on budget documents, raising concerns about how effectively citizens and organisations can engage before the deadline.
The relevant departmental committees will consider all submissions before presenting their reports to the full House for a vote.

The 2027/28 budget carries particular significance, as it will be the final full budget of President William Ruto's first term, with its borrowing levels, spending balance, and revenue measures likely to shape the economic and political environment heading into the 2027 General Election.

items.title: Nikki Germany: When big tech restructures, where does Kenya’s tech talent go next?
items.description: Microsoft
content: Microsoft's reported decision to close its Africa Development Centre (ADC) in Nairobi, seven years after its establishment, has raised fresh questions about Kenya's future as a technology hub. Employees were reportedly informed of the closure on October 12. However, Microsoft has described the changes as part of a global restructuring affecting its engineering operations in Kenya, without confirming a complete shutdown.

For the engineers and other professionals whose livelihoods are affected, this is more than a corporate restructuring. It represents years of experience, professional relationships and work on products used around the world. Their contribution to Kenya’s technology ecosystem should not be overlooked, and neither should the uncertainty facing them and their families. As an industry, we have a responsibility to ensure that their experience is not lost.

Kenya is often described as Africa’s Silicon Savannah, and developments of this nature inevitably raise questions about what that reputation rests on. At Moringa, where we train thousands of young Kenyans for technology careers, we see a bigger question beyond the job losses: has Kenya built an ecosystem and a talent base strong enough to retain and develop world-class engineers when multinationals change direction? Education is central to the answer, because the talent that stays relevant through such shifts is shaped long before a first job.

The ADC’s scale shows why. Announced in 2019 with sites in Nairobi and Lagos, it came with a pledge of $100 million over five years and 500 engineers across both centres by 2023. Nairobi alone had more than 450 full-time employees by March 2022. Kenyan engineers worked in international teams on products built for global markets, and that experience is the investment’s most valuable legacy. Restructuring may eliminate jobs, but it does not erase skills.

It also reminds us that announcements are not outcomes. Microsoft closed its Lagos centre in 2024. That same year, it and UAE-based G42 announced a $1 billion digital investment initiative in Kenya, centred on a proposed geothermal-powered data centre at Olkaria. The project has since stalled, reportedly over power capacity and payment guarantees. None of this means Kenya is losing its appeal, but it exposes the risk of depending on decisions made beyond our borders.

So the real test of Silicon Savannah is what happens when investment changes direction. Can experienced professionals find new opportunities locally, strengthen Kenyan businesses, or build the companies that create the next generation of jobs? Financial services, fintech, telecoms and emerging technology firms can absorb many of them, but salary gaps and fierce competition for global remote roles mean this will not happen automatically. Local employers must offer strong engineering cultures, real career progression and the chance to build competitive products.

That is why education must move beyond job readiness to career resilience. Teaching the technologies employers want today is no longer enough when AI is changing how work is done. At Moringa, we focus on strong technical foundations, so learners understand how software, data, and systems work rather than only today's framework; on problem-solving and product thinking; and on the habit of continuous learning that keeps professionals relevant as employer needs evolve.

Our research shows why. In Moringa’s Graduate Impact Study 2026, 70.9% of surveyed alumni who secured opportunities did so before graduation or within six months. Yet all 14 employers surveyed named technical execution a strength of our graduates, while 63.4% said communication needed to improve. Technical skill gets people hired; communication, business understanding and continuous learning keep them relevant. Our Workforce Capability Report 2026 found that 77% of organisations use online learning platforms, but only 16% rated their upskilling as very effective.

Each partner has a practical role. Employers should offer structured internships and apprenticeships, which accounted for 29.1% of our alumni first opportunities, with real mentorship. They should build technical career ladders that do not force engineers into management, and hire experienced professionals released by restructurings to lead products and mentor juniors.

Education providers should co-design curricula with employers and review them regularly, build learning around real Kenyan problems, teach communication and commercial awareness alongside technical depth, publish graduate outcomes openly, and offer retooling pathways in areas such as AI and cybersecurity for experienced professionals.

Government can make it easier to build and scale from Kenya through predictable tax and regulation, reliable and affordable power, and procurement that gives local technology firms a fair chance. It can reward employers who take on interns, and help founders with early-stage capital and easier cross-border payments, so engineers leaving multinationals can start companies serving global markets from Nairobi.

Microsoft's restructuring is not proof that Silicon Savannah has lost its place in the global technology economy. It is an opportunity to rethink what lasting investment should achieve. The true measure of Kenya's success will not be how many global companies open offices here, but how much local capability remains, grows, and creates new opportunities when they change direction.

Kenya contains imported Ebola case as country moves towards disease-free status
items.description: Kenya contains imported Ebola case as country moves towards disease-free status Kenya Association of Travel Agents
content: Kenya has contained an imported Ebola outbreak without community transmission, with authorities confirming that all patients have recovered or been discharged and the country now entering a 42-day countdown towards an official declaration that it is free of the disease.

The outbreak originated from a Kenyan national who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and travelled through Uganda before arriving in Nairobi on October 3, 2026. The Ministry of Health confirmed the country’s first case of Bundibugyo Ebola Virus Disease on October 6.
The case triggered an extensive public health response involving isolation, laboratory testing, contact tracing and monitoring to prevent further transmission.

Kenya subsequently recorded eight secondary infections, bringing the total to nine confirmed cases. All eight were linked to the initial imported case, involving four family members and four healthcare workers. Crucially, all secondary cases were identified among people already under quarantine, and health authorities reported no transmission into the wider community.
The outbreak resulted in two deaths, while seven patients recovered.

The Ministry of Health identified and monitored 135 contacts linked to the initial case, including individuals in Kenya and abroad. The final patient was discharged on November 11, while the remaining 11 contacts completed their monitoring period without developing symptoms.

The 42-day countdown began on November 12 and, if no new infections are detected, Kenya is expected to be declared Ebola-free on December 23, 2026. The period represents twice the virus’s maximum 21-day incubation period, in line with World Health Organization protocols.

The successful containment effort highlights Kenya’s public health surveillance and emergency response capabilities, including early case detection, laboratory confirmation, isolation facilities, contact tracing and coordination between national and county health authorities.

The World Health Organization has also reported no evidence of transmission outside the identified cluster and no new confirmed cases in Kenya since October 19. In its latest disease outbreak update, the organisation advised against imposing travel or trade restrictions on countries responding to the regional health event.

For Kenya’s travel and tourism industry, the distinction between an imported case and sustained local transmission is particularly important. The outbreak did not result in widespread community transmission or a nationwide shutdown of economic and social activities.

The government has maintained that Kenya remains open for international travel, tourism, trade and business, with no domestic restrictions on movement or public gatherings. Enhanced health screening and surveillance at points of entry remain in place as precautionary measures.

While the outbreak in the DRC continues to require regional vigilance, Kenya’s experience demonstrates the importance of effective disease surveillance and rapid containment in protecting public health and maintaining international travel connectivity.
